title: THE STAR THAT WANTED ITS CHILDREN
deck: Sael has lit three inhabited moons for six billion years. In nineteen days the conscious star intends to spend itself in a flare that will seed a silent nebula—and strip eight billion living people from the worlds already in its light. Illuminara must protect the present without turning a godlike parent into a prisoner.
shape: Five scenes moving from Sael's announced nineteen-day flare and the moons' plan to numb the star, through Illuminara's voluntary encounter with Sael's long memory and her discovery that a narrow chain can preserve what a broad fatal shell was meant to carry, into a costly public bargain, a failed demonstrator in which Sael freely spends an irreplaceable gift to protect living riggers, and a first sail whose proof, correction and renewable stewardship preserve all three moons while beginning the star's chosen gift to the distant nebula.

scenes.title: Nineteen Days of Light
paragraphs: *Assembly vault beneath Lume, innermost moon of Orison · Nineteen days before flare threshold*

Sael filled half the sky through the vault's polar glass. The old star was amber at its quiet edge and white where a magnetic arch rose six hundred thousand kilometres above the surface. Every eleven minutes the arch brightened. Every eleven minutes the vault floor gave a low answering hum, as if the moon had become a tuning fork held against a god's throat.
Eight billion people lived on Lume, Vey and cold Harrow. Their governments had sent twelve delegates, four admirals and one empty chair for the being they had only learned to hear three days ago.

The empty chair spoke first. Its voice came from helioseismic tones translated by instruments around all three moons. The words were not perfectly timed. Sael began some sentences before the translator finished the last, because a star did not think in the order a room preferred.

**Sael**  
Nineteen of your days remain before I cross the useful threshold. Remove your ships from the eastern magnetic road. The particles there will be needed elsewhere.

Minister Aro Venn laid both hands on a black case beside him. Inside it rested the authorization keys for the Quiet Crown, a belt of superconducting stations designed to flatten Sael's magnetic speech and hold the flare below ignition.

**Aro Venn**  
Needed to kill us.

**Sael**  
Needed to make what comes after me possible.

Behind the delegates, a wall map showed the neighboring Oriel Nebula: a dark red wound seven light-years long, rich in hydrogen and poor in everything that could build rock, water or blood. Sael's models said a narrow stream of carbon, oxygen and iron could change that. The same ejection, released all at once, would peel the atmospheres from the moons before it left Orison.

Illuminara stood between the case and the empty chair. She could feel the forces the instruments rendered as coloured lines: the pressure gathering below Sael's photosphere, the magnetic cage waking station by station, the small trembling loads in the vault's roof. Force was legible. Intention was not.

**Illuminara**  
My aim is plain. The three moons keep their atmospheres and every person gets the chance to live. Sael keeps the right to choose what its death means. I will not trade one of those for the other before I understand what is actually required.
Aro opened the black case. The keys were ordinary metal, worn at the edges by rehearsals nobody had expected to use.

**Aro Venn**  
A conscious catastrophe is still a catastrophe. The Crown buys us eighty years. In eighty years we can evacuate or learn to govern it safely.

**Sael**  
You have consumed my light for six billion years and call another eighty years restraint. The nebula has waited without a voice. Its worlds cannot petition your assembly because I have not yet made them.

**Illuminara**  
And the people under your light? What are they to you?
A chain of sunspots crossed Sael's face. The translator hesitated, discarded two approximations and chose a third.

**Sael**  
Passengers. Beautiful ones. Brief ones. They built homes on stones that circle me. They did not ask what I meant to build.

The word passengers moved through the chamber more dangerously than the rising magnetic arch. Harrow's delegate left his seat. In the public gallery, foundry workers began shouting. Aro's thumb settled over the first key.

Illuminara did not ask them to forgive the word. She asked the roof to hold while the shouting found its shape, setting one hand against the vault's central spar as the old stone took a thermal jolt from Sael's brightening arch. Her strength kept dust from falling. It did not make anyone agree.

Wren Odira placed a small mechanical clock on the table. Deep contact with Sael would fold Illuminara's protection inward. During it, she could not hold the vault, stop the Crown or shield a moon. The clock's red hand was set to eight minutes.

**Wren**  
Eight minutes. At seven I call you. At eight I pull the solar link, whether the star has finished its sentence or not.

**Aro Venn**  
And while you listen, what stops it crossing the threshold?

**Sael**  
I do.
For the first time, the translator caught something like anger without delay.

**Illuminara**  
Then that is the first thing you can do for the living: hold the arch for eight minutes because you choose to, not because the Crown makes you. If you cannot, there is no conversation to enter.
Sael's arch continued to rise for six long seconds. Then it bent sideways, poured its fire into a harmless loop and dimmed.
Aro removed his thumb from the key. He did not close the case.

**Sael**  
Eight minutes. Do not ask me to pretend silence is not a life merely because it has not begun.

scenes.title: The Silent Shore
paragraphs: *Solar observatory Thren, high orbit above Sael · Seventeen days before threshold*

The wide window opened only after Sael accepted its terms in three different forms: a magnetic sequence it could verify, a spoken explanation from Illuminara, and the uninterrupted right to end contact. Wren waited outside with the red clock. Aro waited beside the Crown controls. No fleet moved toward the star.

Illuminara entered no human room. She found pressure, convection and time. Sael's thought lived in loops that took weeks to rise and centuries to close. The window did not compress them into human memory; it let her stand near their scale without claiming it as her own.

She saw Orison before the moons had cooled: dark stones crossing a young star's light. She felt six billion years of fusion turn simple matter into the heavier elements Sael carried in its core and shell. Far beyond the system lay Oriel, a cold shore that gathered hydrogen, lost it, gathered it again. In Sael's long attention the nebula was not empty. It was unfinished.
No future people appeared. The field could not certify them. There were only models, patience and Sael's fierce interpretation of what a star owed the universe.

**Sael**  
You will say they are imaginary because they cannot answer.

**Illuminara**  
No. I will say possibility is not permission to kill. Those are different claims.
A convective wall turned beneath them. Its sound was the sound of a continent boiling.

**Sael**  
Your moons cut metals from my children before they cool. They net my wind. They drink the gradient between my heat and their night. They call this living. When I spend what I made on a future they cannot own, they call it death.

**Illuminara**  
They call eight billion deaths death. You keep changing the scale so you do not have to use the number.
The window narrowed. For an instant Illuminara felt Sael preparing to end it. She did not reach for the star's inner force or widen the contact without consent.

**Sael**  
Eight billion present voices against uncounted silent ones. Your arithmetic has already chosen its favorite tense.

It was Sael's strongest argument, and it was not foolish. Every assembly in Orison could promise only the safety of voters who already existed. A magnetic cage would preserve them by taking the only generative choice Sael believed remained. Simple persuasion would ask a being older than their species to treat a century as morally serious while refusing to treat a million years that way.

Illuminara stopped arguing with the flare and examined its work. Sael had shaped it as a broad shell. The breadth was not needed to reach Oriel; it kept the heavy elements together after they crossed the system's chaotic wind. Along the shell's inner edge, each emitting magnetic loop rolled a fraction as it opened, and Sael kept turning the release beneath it so the elements did not drift apart. A wide gift could hide that motion inside its width. A narrow one would remember exactly where the loop had faced. Sael wanted continuity, not explosion for its own sake.

Below them, the inhabited moons moved through the star's memory as three recurring shadows. Around Lume and Vey, freight mirrors already passed fragile loads from one sail to the next. Illuminara followed the handoff in her mind: a chain of catcher sails could do for a narrow pulse what Sael's breadth did for the shell, refocusing each separated band before the system's wind could scatter it. Harrow's foundries could make the mesh. No single sail had to govern the whole journey.

**Illuminara**  
If the elements reached Oriel over a century instead of one day, would their meaning change?

**Sael**  
A century is an oath your species uses for ceremonies and breaks for budgets.

**Illuminara**  
Then do not accept an oath. Accept a mechanism you can stop. One small pulse. One sail. Then another only when the next generation has built its part and asks for it. You keep the power to refuse us. The living keep the power to renew or end the labor.

Sael showed her the weakness at once. The first pulse required a magnetic throat wider than any foundry sail. Constructing it in seventeen days would need the very superconductors already committed to the Crown. The moons would have to surrender their best weapon before they knew the alternative worked.

**Sael**  
They will ask you to build it and call their fear a contribution.

**Illuminara**  
I can lift the first frame and hold it through launch. I cannot manufacture a century of consent. I will not aim your descendants for you. If the foundries and the assemblies will not carry the work, you will know the offer is false.
The red hand reached seven minutes. Wren's voice entered as a thin external line.

**Wren**  
One minute, Nara.
Sael's pressure moved against the edge of the window, curious rather than violent.

**Sael**  
Nara.

**Illuminara**  
My mother still calls me that.

**Sael**  
A name from before your power. You kept it.

**Illuminara**  
Keeping is not the same as refusing to change.
She left before Sael answered. The red hand struck eight as the window closed. Outside, Aro stood over untouched controls. Sael still held the magnetic arch below threshold.
For the first time since arriving, Illuminara felt joy without relief attached to it. The solution was not yet real.

scenes.title: What a Century Costs
paragraphs: *Harrow polar foundry and the linked assemblies · Fourteen days before threshold*

The Quiet Crown's final throat-coil hung over Foundry Nine like a black halo. Melt it down and the foundry could spin the first heliosail: a web two hundred kilometres across, thin enough to move under a controlled pulse and strong enough to sort charged iron from the flare. Keep it intact and the Crown could begin numbing Sael within six hours.

Rian Vale, elected master of the foundry guild, stood under the coil with six hundred workers. Half wore the silver band of the sail proposal. Half wore the black band of the Crown. Her own wrists were bare.

**Rian Vale**  
The sail takes four percent of Orison's foundry output every year for a century. Harrow's east habitats wait eleven more months for radiation roofs. Vey postpones two ocean pumps. Lume gives up half its storm reserve. Do not call this a beautiful promise. Name the people who pay for it.

On the assembly screens, names appeared beside the costs. Habitat cooperatives. Pump crews. The children scheduled to move out of Harrow's oldest caverns. Illuminara had asked for the ledger before asking for a vote. If love for unborn worlds required making living workers invisible, it would repeat Sael's mistake in smaller language.

**Aro Venn**  
A century compact is theatre. The unborn cannot bind themselves. The star can stop the pulses whenever it chooses, while we cannot recover a melted Crown in time.

**Illuminara**  
Then the compact must not bind the unborn. Every eleven years each moon renews its contribution separately. If one refuses, no punishment, no forced pulse. The material already built remains theirs. Sael receives no claim on future labor—only evidence each generation may offer again.

**Aro Venn**  
You have made the chain optional. That makes it incredible to Sael.
Rian turned to the workers rather than the screens.

**Rian Vale**  
And the first sail? Honesty will not spin two hundred kilometres of mesh in fourteen days.

Illuminara unfolded a physical plan across the floor. Foundry Nine would spin forty modular ribbons. Existing storm tugs would carry them sunward. Illuminara could hold the joining frame against Sael's wind for sixty-one seconds during launch, no longer; after that, ordinary tension and the guild's control vanes had to keep it open. Three unmanned catcher sails would trace the outbound stream. If captured mass fell below ninety-nine point seven percent, or radiation at any moon rose above its ordinary storm limit, Sael would end the pulse and the experiment would count as failed.

The proof had a clock. Sael would emit the test pulse on threshold day. The sail would have six minutes to separate its charge bands and forty hours to show a stable course toward Oriel. The Crown would remain partly assembled until the moment the throat-coil was needed for the sail.
Tavi Sen, a young rigger from Harrow's east habitats, raised a black-banded wrist.

**Tavi Sen**  
My family has moved their roof date three times. You want us to delay it for worlds that may never exist. What do we receive besides the honor of being reasonable?
A murmur ran through the workers. Rian did not silence it.

**Illuminara**  
A real roof date funded first from Lume's storm reserve, and a veto if it slips. No moon gets to buy the future with Harrow's present. The sail design also returns its induced current to the east grid after each pulse. Not enough to erase the cost. Enough to make the same structure protect the people building it.

**Tavi Sen**  
And if Lume votes no after we melt our coil?

**Aro Venn**  
Then I have failed at the one job for which this case was put in my hands.

Aro touched the authorization case. He had been a child during the Red Eruption, when an ordinary storm burned Vey's northern sky and killed his older sister in a shelter whose door fused shut. The Crown was not a politician's appetite for control. It was the only answer he had spent thirty years making ready.

**Aro Venn**  
You ask me to place eight billion people behind a test whose other party can become angry enough to boil rock.

**Sael**  
You planned to make me unable to be angry and named that safety.
The translated voice came through the foundry floor. Workers stepped away from the coil as its shadow trembled.

**Aro Venn**  
I planned to keep children from learning the sound a shelter makes when its door melts.

**Sael**  
And I planned to keep a nebula from remaining a shelter with no children in it.

The argument did not reconcile them. Illuminara did not turn Aro's grief into a reason he had to yield. She put his condition into the test: until capture crossed ninety-nine point seven percent, three Crown stations would remain active as emergency deflectors under separate keys held by the moon assemblies. They could protect the moons from the trial pulse but could not reach deep enough to silence Sael.
Rian called the votes. Lume accepted. Vey accepted after its patient councils won priority on the returned sail current. Harrow divided exactly in half.
Tavi removed his black wristband. He did not put on silver.

**Tavi Sen**  
Show us the star can spend power on our safety before it asks us to spend our roof on its future.
The vote remained tied. No coil melted. The proposal had met the one objection no design could solve on paper.
Sael's magnetic arch brightened above the polar glass. It had listened to the cost being named. Whether it had understood was still unproved.

scenes.title: The Pulse Sael Kept
paragraphs: *Sunward construction orbit · Nine days before threshold*

They built a smaller demonstrator without the throat-coil. It could not launch material toward Oriel. It could only prove that Sael and the foundries could shape a pulse together without harming the moons.
Rian called it a toy. Aro called it insufficient. Tavi volunteered to rig it because neither word made the test useless.

Four storm tugs stretched the mesh into a shining square thirty kilometres wide. Illuminara held the central frame while the riggers locked its vanes. Sael lowered a filament of charged carbon toward it, gentle by stellar measure and large enough to turn night into blue day across Harrow.
Wren counted down from the observatory while the Crown deflectors and Harrow shelters reported ready. At forty seconds, her voice left only the clock in Illuminara's ear.

**Aro Venn**  
If the pulse exceeds the agreed band, I call for all three keys.

**Sael**  
If you turn them before it does, I end this conversation.

**Illuminara**  
Both statements stand. No one improves them by pretending trust already exists.

At twenty-one seconds, the outer ribbon twisted. A manufacture seam that had passed every cold inspection began to unzip under solar charge. The failure travelled inward faster than the tugs could release tension. Tavi and two riggers were clipped to the failing quadrant.
Illuminara could keep the frame open or gather the three workers into her protection. Deep in Sael's wind, she could not do both. She released the frame.

The square folded. She crossed thirty kilometres before the torn ribbon completed its first turn, wrapped her field around the riggers and pushed their tug clear. Behind her, the uncontrolled mesh presented its full conductive face to the incoming filament.
At Aro's call, Lume's assembly turned its key. Lume's deflector woke. The other two keys waited for Vey and Harrow.

**Aro Venn**  
Sael, end the pulse.

**Sael**  
Its structure is already above you. Ending the source does not end what travels.

**Aro Venn**  
Then turn it.

**Sael**  
That carbon took eleven thousand years to raise into this loop.
Tavi's suit spun within Illuminara's field. Through the transparent faceplate, his eyes stayed fixed on the blue-white filament bearing down on the moons.

**Tavi Sen**  
Minister, turn the rest.
Vey's key turned. Harrow's did not. Rian held it in the foundry chamber, waiting the final second the test allowed Sael to choose.

Through the bounded window, Sael felt Illuminara's field fold tight around three brief lives and saw, in Tavi's faceplate, fear aimed past himself toward the moons; behind them, the frame she had promised to hold tumbled free.
Sael changed.

The convective road Illuminara had entered days before contracted around the filament. Magnetic arches fell across one another, not as a cage imposed from outside but as a hand closing over its own gift. The filament spread into a pale aurora too thin to damage atmosphere or sail. Eleven thousand years of gathered material diffused into light that no nebula would inherit.
The torn demonstrator drifted harmlessly past Harrow. The Crown's instruments measured the result: less radiation than an ordinary winter storm.
Rian took her hand off the third key.
For six minutes Sael did not speak.

**Tavi Sen**  
You could have let the deflectors take it.

**Sael**  
Two were awake. One was waiting to know me.

**Tavi Sen**  
I was waiting to know you.

**Sael**  
Now we have each wasted something irreplaceable on the other's uncertainty.
Tavi laughed once, breathlessly. It was not forgiveness, but it was the first sound in the exchange that belonged to neither fear nor grandeur.
Rian reconvened Harrow's vote. Aro asked to speak before it.

**Aro Venn**  
Keep two Crown stations as deflectors. Melt the throat-coil for the full sail. Renew the compact every eleven years, exactly as proposed. If any assembly withdraws, Sael suspends the next pulse. If Sael breaks the capture limit, the stations protect the moons.

**Sael**  
You still prepare against me.

**Aro Venn**  
Yes. Keep both shields. Test the compact again in eleven years.
The arch over Sael's surface rose and settled.

**Sael**  
Keep the Lume and Vey shields.

Harrow voted sixty-one percent for the sail. Tavi voted yes after the habitat roof fund transferred into an account the east cooperatives controlled. Rian gave the order. Foundry cutters entered the black throat-coil and began turning a weapon of silence into forty ribbons of listening metal. They ran three shifts and carried the demonstrator's repaired seam pattern into every ribbon to recover the five days the tied vote had cost.

scenes.title: A Gift That Can Be Refused
paragraphs: *The first heliosail beyond Harrow · Threshold day and forty hours later*

The full sail opened like a dark flower against Sael. Forty ribbons joined at a ring built from the throat-coil. Ordinary tugs held thirty-nine. Illuminara held the last while Rian's crews repaired the demonstrator's failed seam pattern across two hundred kilometres of mesh.
At sixty-one seconds, Illuminara released the frame.
It stayed open.

No cheer came yet. The proof remained the one Harrow had voted on: capture at or above ninety-nine point seven percent, no moon exposed beyond an ordinary storm, and a course the catchers could hold. The three assemblies, the foundry guild and Sael each retained a stop signal. The Lume and Vey Crown stations waited as shields, their deep-field circuits dismantled.

**Wren**  
All parties show green. Sael, the path is yours to begin and yours to end.

**Sael**  
Not mine alone.

A warm pressure touched the sail. Carbon arrived first, then oxygen, silicon and a thin bright thread of iron. The mesh sorted their charges into nested bands while amber light crossed the night side of every moon.

The sail's induced current poured into Harrow's east grid. In the oldest cavern, radiation-roof printers started months before their revised schedule. Tavi watched their load line from a tug, one hand still resting over the patched seam.

The capture line climbed past its red mark. The lost fraction dispersed above the moons' orbital plane, and radiation stayed below winter-storm level. One by one the catcher sails took the separated bands and began the long bend toward Oriel.
Still no one cheered. The course display needed forty hours to distinguish a stable path from a beautiful mistake.

Sael used the wait to slow the deeper magnetic arch. District by district, the evacuation alarms went dark, but the work inside the star was not quiet. Great loops that Sael had spent ages arranging collapsed into harmless light.

**Sael**  
I made one day carry everything I meant by parent. I am taking it apart layer by layer. Your instruments call that safety. They cannot name what disappears.
Illuminara did not answer with another design. She asked Wren to pass the navigation watch to Aro, opened the same bounded solar window Sael could end, and stayed while the first arch fell.

**Illuminara**  
Then let me witness it without renaming it. Tell me what you meant each part to become.

For most of an hour Sael showed her no future people, only intended elements, pressures and distances. One collapsed loop had been tuned to send iron last into a young world's turning core, keeping its first ocean warm beneath a faint sun. Illuminara held the sequence without compressing it and asked why the iron must arrive after the silicates. Sael showed her the timing twice.

When the window closed, the assemblies' displays showed three separate eleven-year commitments, each with its own renewal light. Nebula advocates took seats beside habitat cooperatives, and Sael and every moon kept a stop signal.

At hour thirty-nine, the projected stream began to wander. On the display, the nested bands stepped sideways in the same cadence Illuminara had felt inside Sael: the pulse was remembering the magnetic loop that had released it.

**Illuminara**  
It did not leave a point. The loop turned beneath it. Aro, use the final angle Sael showed the sail.
Aro was already laying the rotation over the catcher geometry. His correction kept the second sail inside its remaining reach.

**Aro Venn**  
The second catcher can still hold it if Sael gives us the loop's final angle.

**Sael**  
You intend to improve my aim.

**Aro Venn**  
I intend to keep your gift from becoming empty weather.
Sael transmitted the angle. Aro sent the correction. At forty hours, the three catcher sails settled onto a stable path whose uncertainty cone lay entirely inside Oriel's hydrogen shelf.

Then the system cheered. It began in Foundry Nine, where cutters struck their tools against the empty supports of the Crown. It crossed assembly galleries and hospital corridors. It reached the old cavern as the first roof panel came hot from its printer. Even the translator carried the vibration back to Sael.

**Sael**  
Is this how passengers sound when they decide where the vessel goes?

**Illuminara**  
Listen to them. They chose the course with you.

**Sael**  
Do not call the silent worlds less real now that you have saved the speaking ones.

**Illuminara**  
I will not. And do not call the speaking ones passengers again.
Sael took seven human seconds to answer, a deliberate delay from a mind that could use centuries.

**Sael**  
Crew, then. Difficult crew.

The first pulse was too small to make a planet, and no one could prove Oriel would ever wake. Four percent of Orison's foundries would serve the chain. Sael would die earlier than the moons wanted. Aro kept two shields because one brave choice did not erase the reason he had built them. Tavi's family still had months of roofing ahead.
Wren found Illuminara seated on the observatory hull after the celebrations thinned, both hands against the warm metal. Wren said nothing; she set her palm beside one of Illuminara's.
Sael was correcting the next pulse with Aro's navigation team; each adjustment came through the metal as a low warm hum. Far beyond sight, three small sails held their line toward Oriel.

critic_line: Sael, a star that has lit three inhabited moons for six billion years, is neither silenced nor forced into a one-day flare: Illuminara's reading of what it wanted to leave behind becomes a stoppable pulse the moons can renew or end, and the first catcher sails hold their course toward Oriel.

shared_strengths: A conscious star with a moral case for its own death is a strong, humane premise with dialogue-driven negotiation. Technical and procedural density (percentages, clocks, keys, sail mechanics) and a tidy, collaborative resolution may tire some readers, but the closing 'Crew, then. Difficult crew.' lands well.

A morally serious, emotionally legible dilemma, memorable star voice, and earned negotiated resolution should strongly engage this audience. The dialogue carries abstract ethics well, though the long technical-policy middle and specialized sail mechanics may slow some readers before the excellent failed demonstration restores urgency.

Reading slowed at: Along the shell's inner edge, each emitting magnetic loop rolled a fraction as it opened, and Sael kept turning the release beneath it so the elements did not drift apart.

translation_sl.title: ZVEZDA, KI JE HOTELA SVOJE OTROKE
translation_sl.deck: Sael že šest milijard let osvetljuje tri naseljene lune. Čez devetnajst dni se namerava zavestna zvezda porabiti v izbruhu, ki bo zasejal tiho meglico — in osmim milijardam živih ljudi odvzel svetove, ki so že v njeni svetlobi. Illuminara mora zaščititi sedanjost, ne da bi bogovsko starševsko bitje spremenila v ujetnico.
translation_sl.shape: Pet prizorov vodi od Saelinega napovedanega izbruha čez devetnajst dni in načrta lun, da zvezdo omrtvijo, prek Illuminaričinega prostovoljnega srečanja s Saelinim dolgim spominom in njenega odkritja, da lahko ozka veriga ohrani tisto, kar naj bi nosila široka smrtonosna lupina, do dragega javnega dogovora, spodletelega demonstratorja, pri katerem Sael svobodno porabi nenadomestljivo darilo, da zaščiti žive monterje, ter prvega jadra, katerega dokaz, popravek in obnovljivo skrbništvo ohranijo vse tri lune, hkrati pa začnejo zvezdino izbrano darilo oddaljeni meglici.

scenes.title: Devetnajst dni svetlobe
paragraphs: *Zbornični obok pod Lume, najbolj notranjo luno Orisona · devetnajst dni pred pragom izbruha*

Sael je skozi polarno steklo oboka zapolnjevala polovico neba. Stara zvezda je bila ob mirnem robu jantarna, tam, kjer se je magnetni lok dvigal šeststo tisoč kilometrov nad površino, pa bela. Vsakih enajst minut je lok zasijal močneje. Vsakih enajst minut je tla oboka napolnil nizek odgovor, kakor da je luna postala glasbene vilice, pritisnjene ob grlo boga.

Na Lume, Vey in mrzlem Harrowu je živelo osem milijard ljudi. Njihove vlade so poslale dvanajst delegatov, štiri admirale in en prazen stol za bitje, ki so se ga naučili slišati šele pred tremi dnevi.

Prazen stol je spregovoril prvi. Njegov glas je prihajal iz helioseizmičnih tonov, ki so jih prevajali instrumenti okoli vseh treh lun. Besede niso bile povsem časovno usklajene. Sael je nekatere stavke začela, še preden je prevajalnik končal prejšnjega, kajti zvezda ni razmišljala v zaporedju, ki bi ustrezalo sobi.

**Sael**  
Še devetnajst vaših dni, preden prestopim uporabni prag. Umaknite ladje z vzhodne magnetne poti. Tamkajšnji delci bodo potrebni drugje.

Minister Aro Venn je obe dlani položil na črn kovček ob sebi. V njem so ležali ključi za odobritev Tihe krone, pasu superprevodnih postaj, zasnovanih tako, da zravnajo Saelin magnetni govor in zadržijo izbruh pod točko vžiga.

**Aro Venn**  
Potrebni, da nas ubijejo.

**Sael**  
Potrebni, da omogočijo tisto, kar pride za menoj.

Za delegati je stenski zemljevid kazal sosednjo meglico Oriel: temno rdečo rano, dolgo sedem svetlobnih let, bogato z vodikom in revno z vsem, iz česar bi bilo mogoče zgraditi skalo, vodo ali kri. Saelini modeli so kazali, da bi jo ozek tok ogljika, kisika in železa lahko spremenil. Isti izmet, sproščen naenkrat, bi lunam odtrgal ozračje, še preden bi zapustil Orison.

Illuminara je stala med kovčkom in praznim stolom. Čutila je sile, ki so jih instrumenti risali kot obarvane črte: pritisk, ki se je zbiral pod Saelino fotosfero, magnetno kletko, ki se je prebujala postajo za postajo, drobna trepetajoča bremena v strehi oboka. Silo je bilo mogoče brati. Namere ne.

**Illuminara**  
Moj cilj je jasen. Vse tri lune obdržijo svoja ozračja in vsak človek dobi možnost živeti. Sael obdrži pravico odločiti, kaj pomeni njena smrt. Nobenega od tega ne bom zamenjala za drugo, preden ne razumem, kaj je dejansko potrebno.
Aro je odprl črni kovček. Ključi so bili iz navadne kovine, njihovi robovi pa obrabljeni od vaj, za katere nihče ni pričakoval, da bodo kdaj potrebne.

**Aro Venn**  
Zavestna katastrofa je še vedno katastrofa. Krona nam kupi osemdeset let. V osemdesetih letih se lahko evakuiramo ali naučimo, kako jo varno obvladovati.

**Sael**  
Šest milijard let ste uživali mojo svetlobo, dodatnih osemdeset let pa imenujete zadržanost. Meglica je čakala brez glasu. Njeni svetovi ne morejo prositi vaše skupščine, ker jih še nisem ustvarila.

**Illuminara**  
Kaj pa ljudje pod tvojo svetlobo? Kaj so zate oni?
Čez Saelin obraz je zdrsnila veriga sončnih peg. Prevajalnik je okleval, zavrgel dva približka in izbral tretjega.

**Sael**  
Potniki. Čudoviti potniki. Kratkotrajni. Domove so zgradili na kamnih, ki krožijo okoli mene. Niso vprašali, kaj sem nameravala zgraditi jaz.
Beseda potniki je prešla skozi dvorano nevarneje kot dvigajoči se magnetni lok. Harrowov delegat je vstal. V javni galeriji so livarski delavci začeli vpiti. Arov palec je obstal nad prvim ključem.

Illuminara jih ni prosila, naj besedo odpustijo. Prosila je streho, naj zdrži, medtem ko je kričanje dobivalo obliko, in eno roko naslonila na osrednji nosilec oboka, ko je stari kamen sprejel toplotni sunek Saelinega vse svetlejšega loka. Njena moč je preprečila, da bi padal prah. Nikogar ni prisilila v strinjanje.

Wren Odira je na mizo postavila majhno mehansko uro. Globok stik s Sael bi Illuminaričino zaščito obrnil navznoter. Med njim ne bi mogla držati oboka, ustaviti Krone ali zaščititi lune. Rdeči kazalec ure je nastavila na osem minut.

**Wren**  
Osem minut. Ob sedmih te pokličem. Ob osmih prekinem sončno povezavo, ne glede na to, ali je zvezda dokončala stavek ali ne.

**Aro Venn**  
In kaj ji med tvojim poslušanjem preprečuje, da prestopi prag?

**Sael**  
Jaz.
Prevajalnik je prvič brez zamude ujel nekaj, kar je spominjalo na jezo.

**Illuminara**  
Potem je to prva stvar, ki jo lahko narediš za žive: lok zadrži osem minut, ker si se tako odločila, ne zato, ker te Krona sili. Če tega ne zmoreš, ni pogovora, v katerega bi lahko vstopili.
Saelin lok se je še šest dolgih sekund dvigal. Nato se je upognil vstran, izlil svoj ogenj v neškodljivo zanko in potemnel.
Aro je umaknil palec s ključa. Kovčka ni zaprl.

**Sael**  
Osem minut. Ne prosi me, naj se pretvarjam, da tišina ni življenje samo zato, ker se še ni začela.

scenes.title: Tiha obala
paragraphs: *Sončni observatorij Thren, visoka orbita nad Sael · sedemnajst dni pred pragom*

Široko okno se je odprlo šele potem, ko je Sael njegove pogoje sprejela v treh različnih oblikah: z magnetnim zaporedjem, ki ga je lahko preverila, z Illuminaričino govorjeno razlago in z neprekinjeno pravico, da stik konča. Wren je čakala zunaj z rdečo uro. Aro je čakal ob upravljanju Krone. Nobena flota se ni premaknila proti zvezdi.

Illuminara ni vstopila v nobeno človeško sobo. Našla je pritisk, konvekcijo in čas. Saelina misel je živela v zankah, ki so potrebovale tedne, da so se dvignile, in stoletja, da so se sklenile. Okno jih ni stisnilo v človeški spomin; omogočilo ji je stati ob njihovem merilu, ne da bi ga razglasila za svojega.

Videla je Orison, preden so se lune ohladile: temni kamni so prečkali svetlobo mlade zvezde. Začutila je šest milijard let fuzije, ki je preprosto snov spreminjala v težje elemente, ki jih je Sael nosila v jedru in lupini. Daleč onkraj sistema je ležal Oriel, mrzla obala, ki je zbirala vodik, ga izgubljala in znova zbirala. V Saelini dolgi pozornosti meglica ni bila prazna. Bila je nedokončana.
Nobeni prihodnji ljudje se niso prikazali. Polje jih ni moglo potrditi. Obstajali so samo modeli, potrpežljivost in Saelina silovita razlaga tega, kar zvezda dolguje vesolju.

**Sael**  
Rekla boš, da so namišljeni, ker ne morejo odgovoriti.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Rekla bom, da možnost ni dovoljenje za ubijanje. To sta različni trditvi.
Pod njima se je obrnila konvekcijska stena. Zvenela je kot celina, ki vre.

**Sael**  
Vaše lune režejo kovine iz mojih otrok, še preden se ohladijo. Lovijo moj veter. Pijejo razliko med mojo vročino in svojo nočjo. Temu pravijo življenje. Ko porabim, kar sem ustvarila, za prihodnost, ki je ne morejo posedovati, temu pravijo smrt.

**Illuminara**  
Smrt osmih milijard sedanjih glasov imenujejo smrt. Nenehno spreminjaš merilo, da ti ni treba uporabiti številke.
Okno se je zožilo. Illuminara je za hip začutila, da se Sael pripravlja stik končati. Ni segla po zvezdini notranji sili niti brez soglasja razširila stika.

**Sael**  
Osem milijard sedanjih glasov proti nepreštetim tihim. Tvoja aritmetika si je že izbrala najljubši čas.

To je bil Saelin najmočnejši argument in ni bil neumen. Vsaka skupščina v Orisonu je lahko obljubila samo varnost volivcem, ki so že obstajali. Magnetna kletka bi jih ohranila tako, da bi Sael odvzela edino ustvarjalno izbiro, za katero je verjela, da ji je ostala. Preprosto prepričevanje bi bitje, starejše od njihove vrste, prosilo, naj ima stoletje za moralno pomembno, hkrati pa zavračalo, da bi enako obravnavalo milijon let.

Illuminara se je nehala prepirati z izbruhom in preučila njegovo delo. Sael ga je oblikovala kot široko lupino. Širina ni bila potrebna, da bi dosegel Oriel; težke elemente je držala skupaj, potem ko so prečkali kaotični veter sistema. Ob notranjem robu lupine se je vsaka magnetna zanka ob odprtju malo zavrtela, Sael pa je sproščanje pod njo obračala naprej, da se elementi niso razpršili. Široko darilo je lahko to gibanje skrilo v svoji širini. Ozko bi si natančno zapomnilo, kam je bila zanka obrnjena. Sael je hotela zveznost, ne eksplozije zaradi nje same.

Pod njima so naseljene lune potovale skozi zvezdin spomin kot tri ponavljajoče se sence. Okoli Lume in Veya so tovorna zrcala že predajala krhka bremena z enega jadra na drugo. Illuminara je v mislih sledila predaji: veriga lovilnih jader bi lahko za ozek sunek storila to, kar je Saelina širina naredila za lupino, in znova zbrala vsak ločeni pas, preden bi ga veter sistema lahko razpršil. Harrowove livarne bi lahko izdelale mrežo. Nobenemu posameznemu jadru ne bi bilo treba upravljati celotne poti.

**Illuminara**  
Če bi elementi dosegli Oriel v stoletju namesto v enem dnevu, bi se njihov pomen spremenil?

**Sael**  
Stoletje je prisega, ki jo vaša vrsta uporablja za slovesnosti in krši zaradi proračunov.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ne sprejmi prisege. Sprejmi mehanizem, ki ga lahko ustaviš. En majhen sunek. Eno jadro. Nato naslednjega samo, ko bo prihodnja generacija zgradila svoj del in ga prosila. Obdržiš moč, da nas zavrneš. Živi obdržijo moč, da delo obnovijo ali končajo.

Sael ji je takoj pokazala šibkost. Prvi sunek je potreboval magnetno grlo, širše od kateregakoli livarskega jadra. Za njegovo izdelavo v sedemnajstih dneh bi potrebovali prav tiste superprevodnike, ki so že bili namenjeni Kroni. Lune bi se morale odpovedati svojemu najboljšemu orožju, preden bi vedele, ali alternativa deluje.

**Sael**  
Prosili te bodo, da ga zgradiš, in svoj strah imenovali prispevek.

**Illuminara**  
Prvi okvir lahko dvignem in ga držim med izstrelitvijo. Ne morem izdelati stoletja soglasja. Tvojih potomcev ne bom usmerjala namesto tebe. Če livarne in skupščine ne bodo nosile dela, boš vedela, da je ponudba lažna.
Rdeči kazalec je dosegel sedem minut. Wrenin glas je vstopil kot tanka zunanja črta.

**Wren**  
Še ena minuta, Nara.
Saelin pritisk se je dotaknil roba okna, radoveden, ne nasilen.

**Sael**  
Nara.

**Illuminara**  
Mama me še vedno tako kliče.

**Sael**  
Ime iz časa pred tvojo močjo. Ohranila si ga.

**Illuminara**  
Ohraniti ni isto kot zavrniti spremembo.
Odšla je, preden je Sael odgovorila. Rdeči kazalec je udaril osem, ko se je okno zaprlo. Zunaj je Aro stal nad nedotaknjenim upravljanjem. Sael je magnetni lok še vedno zadrževala pod pragom.
Illuminara je prvič po prihodu občutila veselje, ki mu ni bila pripeta olajšava. Rešitev še ni bila resnična.

scenes.title: Koliko stane stoletje
paragraphs: *Harrowova polarna livarna in povezane skupščine · štirinajst dni pred pragom*

Končna grlna tuljava Tihe krone je visela nad Livarno devet kakor črn svetniški sij. Če bi jo stalili, bi livarna lahko spletla prvo sončno jadro: dvesto kilometrov široko mrežo, dovolj tanko, da se premakne pod nadzorovanim sunkom, in dovolj močno, da iz izbruha loči nabito železo. Če bi jo ohranili nedotaknjeno, bi Krona lahko začela omrtvljati Sael v šestih urah.
Rian Vale, izvoljena vodja livarskega ceha, je stala pod tuljavo s šeststo delavci. Polovica jih je nosila srebrni trak predloga jadra. Polovica črni trak Krone. Njeni zapestji sta bili goli.

**Rian Vale**  
Jadro bo stoletje vsako leto vzelo štiri odstotke livarske proizvodnje Orisona. Harrowovi vzhodni habitati na sevalne strehe čakajo še enajst mesecev. Vey odloži dve oceanski črpalki. Lume se odpove polovici rezerve za nevihte. Ne imenujte tega čudovita obljuba. Poimenujte ljudi, ki jo plačajo.

Na skupščinskih zaslonih so se ob stroških pojavila imena. Stanovanjske zadruge. Ekipe pri črpalkah. Otroci, ki naj bi se preselili iz Harrowovih najstarejših votlin. Illuminara je zahtevala knjigo stroškov, še preden je prosila za glasovanje. Če bi ljubezen do nerojenih svetov zahtevala, da živi delavci postanejo nevidni, bi v manjšem jeziku ponovila Saelino napako.

**Aro Venn**  
Stoletni dogovor je gledališče. Nerojeni se ne morejo zavezati. Zvezda lahko sunke ustavi, kadarkoli se odloči, mi pa staljene Krone ne moremo pravočasno obnoviti.

**Illuminara**  
Potem dogovor nerojenih ne sme zavezovati. Vsakih enajst let vsaka luna ločeno obnovi svoj prispevek. Če katera odstopi, ni kazni in ni prisilnega sunka. Že zgrajeni material ostane njihov. Sael ne dobi pravice do prihodnjega dela — le dokaze, ki jih lahko vsaka generacija znova ponudi.

**Aro Venn**  
Verigo si naredila neobvezno. Zaradi tega je za Sael neverodostojna.
Rian se je obrnila k delavcem, ne k zaslonom.

**Rian Vale**  
Kaj pa prvo jadro? Poštenost ne bo spletla dvesto kilometrov mreže v štirinajstih dneh.

Illuminara je po tleh razgrnila fizični načrt. Livarna devet bi spletla štirideset modularnih trakov. Obstoječi nevihtni vlačilci bi jih ponesli proti soncu. Illuminara bi lahko združevalni okvir med izstrelitvijo držala proti Saelinemu vetru enainšestdeset sekund, nič dlje; nato bi ga morale odprtega držati običajna napetost in cehovske krmilne lopute. Tri brezposadkovna lovilna jadra bi sledila izhodnemu toku. Če bi delež ujete mase padel pod devetindevetdeset celih sedem odstotka ali bi sevanje na kateri od lun preseglo njeno običajno nevihtno mejo, bi Sael sunek končala in poskus bi veljal za neuspešnega.

Dokaz je imel uro. Sael bi preizkusni sunek oddala na dan praga. Jadro bi imelo šest minut, da loči pasove naboja, in štirideset ur, da pokaže stabilno smer proti Orielu. Krona bi ostala delno sestavljena do trenutka, ko bi bila grlna tuljava potrebna za jadro.
Tavi Sen, mladi monter iz Harrowovih vzhodnih habitatov, je dvignil zapestje s črnim trakom.

**Tavi Sen**  
Moja družina je datum strehe prestavila trikrat. Hočete, da ga še enkrat odložimo zaradi svetov, ki morda nikoli ne bodo obstajali. Kaj dobimo poleg časti, da smo razumni?
Med delavci je završalo. Rian jih ni utišala.

**Illuminara**  
Pravi datum strehe, najprej financiran iz Lumine nevihtne rezerve, in veto, če se zamakne. Nobena luna ne sme kupiti prihodnosti s Harrowovo sedanjostjo. Zasnova jadra po vsakem sunku tudi vrača inducirani tok v vzhodno omrežje. Ne dovolj, da bi izbrisala strošek. Dovolj, da ista struktura zaščiti ljudi, ki jo gradijo.

**Tavi Sen**  
Kaj pa, če Lume glasuje proti, potem ko stalimo tuljavo?

**Aro Venn**  
Potem mi ni uspelo pri edini nalogi, zaradi katere je ta kovček pristal v mojih rokah.

Aro se je dotaknil kovčka za odobritev. Med Rdečim izbruhom je bil otrok, ko je navadna nevihta zažgala severno nebo Veya in ubila njegovo starejšo sestro v zaklonišču, katerega vrata so se zvarila. Krona ni bila politikova sla po nadzoru. Bila je edini odgovor, ki ga je pripravljal trideset let.

**Aro Venn**  
Prosiš me, naj osem milijard ljudi postavim za preizkus, katerega druga stran se lahko tako razjezi, da zavre skalo.

**Sael**  
Načrtoval si, da mi onemogočiš jezo, in to poimenoval varnost.
Prevedeni glas je prihajal skozi tla livarne. Delavci so se odmaknili od tuljave, ko je njena senca zatrepetala.

**Aro Venn**  
Načrtoval sem, da otrokom ne bo treba spoznati zvoka zaklonišča, ko se njegova vrata topijo.

**Sael**  
Jaz pa sem načrtovala, da meglica ne bo ostala zaklonišče brez otrok.

Prepir ju ni spravil. Illuminara Arove žalosti ni spremenila v razlog, zaradi katerega bi moral popustiti. Njegov pogoj je vgradila v preizkus: dokler zajem ne preseže devetindevetdeset celih sedem odstotka, tri postaje Krone ostanejo dejavne kot zasilni odklonilniki pod ločenimi ključi, ki jih držijo lunine skupščine. Lune bi lahko zaščitile pred poskusnim sunkom, vendar ne bi segle dovolj globoko, da bi utišale Sael.
Rian je sklicala glasovanje. Lume je sprejela. Vey je sprejel, potem ko so sveti bolnikov dobili prednost pri vrnjenem toku jadra. Harrow se je razdelil natančno na pol.
Tavi je snel črni trak z zapestja. Srebrnega si ni nadel.

**Tavi Sen**  
Pokažite nam, da lahko zvezda porabi moč za našo varnost, preden nas prosi, naj svojo streho porabimo za njeno prihodnost.
Glasovanje je ostalo izenačeno. Nobena tuljava se ni stalila. Predlog je naletel na edini ugovor, ki ga nobena zasnova ni mogla rešiti na papirju.
Saelin magnetni lok je nad polarnim steklom zasijal močneje. Poslušala je, ko so poimenovali ceno. Ali jo je razumela, še ni bilo dokazano.

scenes.title: Sunek, ki ga je Sael zadržala
paragraphs: *Gradbena orbita proti soncu · devet dni pred pragom*
Zgradili so manjši demonstrator brez grlne tuljave. Snovi ni mogel izstreliti proti Orielu. Dokazal je lahko le, da lahko Sael in livarne skupaj oblikujejo sunek, ne da bi poškodovale lune.
Rian mu je rekla igrača. Aro nezadosten. Tavi se je javil, da ga bo sestavil, ker zaradi nobene od teh besed preizkus ni postal nekoristen.

Štirje nevihtni vlačilci so mrežo raztegnili v svetleč kvadrat, širok trideset kilometrov. Illuminara je držala osrednji okvir, medtem ko so monterji zaklepali njegove lopute. Sael je proti njemu spustila nit nabitega ogljika, nežno po zvezdnem merilu in dovolj veliko, da je noč čez Harrow spremenila v moder dan.

Wren je odštevala iz observatorija, medtem ko so odklonilniki Krone in Harrowova zaklonišča sporočali pripravljenost. Pri štiridesetih sekundah je njen glas izginil in v Illuminaričinem ušesu pustil samo uro.

**Aro Venn**  
Če sunek preseže dogovorjeni pas, zahtevam vse tri ključe.

**Sael**  
Če jih obrnete, preden ga preseže, končam ta pogovor.

**Illuminara**  
Obe izjavi veljata. Nihče ju ne izboljša s pretvarjanjem, da zaupanje že obstaja.

Pri enaindvajsetih sekundah se je zunanji trak zvil. Izdelovalni šiv, ki je prestal vsak hladni pregled, se je pod sončnim nabojem začel parati. Okvara je potovala navznoter hitreje, kot so lahko vlačilci sprostili napetost. Tavi in dva monterja so bili pripeti na propadajoči kvadrant.
Illuminara je lahko okvir obdržala odprt ali pa tri delavce zajela v svojo zaščito. Globoko v Saelinem vetru ni mogla obojega. Izpustila je okvir.

Kvadrat se je zložil. Trideset kilometrov je prečkala, še preden je raztrgani trak dokončal prvi obrat, ovila svoje polje okoli monterjev in njihov vlačilec potisnila na varno. Za njo je nenadzorovana mreža prihajajoči niti nastavila vso svojo prevodno površino.
Na Arov poziv je Lumina skupščina obrnila svoj ključ. Lumin odklonilnik se je prebudil. Druga dva ključa sta čakala na Vey in Harrow.

**Aro Venn**  
Sael, končaj sunek.

**Sael**  
Njegova struktura je že nad vami. Končati vir ne pomeni končati tega, kar potuje.

**Aro Venn**  
Potem ga obrni.

**Sael**  
Enajst tisoč let je trajalo, da sem ta ogljik dvignila v to zanko.
Tavijeva obleka se je vrtela v Illuminaričinem polju. Skozi prozorno obrazno ploščo so njegove oči ostale uprte v modro-belo nit, ki se je spuščala nad lune.

**Tavi Sen**  
Minister, obrnite preostala.
Veyev ključ se je obrnil. Harrowov se ni. Rian ga je držala v livarski dvorani in čakala zadnjo sekundo, ki jo je preizkus dal Sael za odločitev.

Skozi omejeno okno je Sael začutila Illuminaričino polje, tesno zloženo okoli treh kratkih življenj, in v Tavijevi obrazni plošči zagledala strah, usmerjen mimo njega proti lunam; za njimi je okvir, ki ga je obljubila držati, prosto padal.
Sael se je spremenila.

Konvekcijska pot, na katero je Illuminara vstopila pred dnevi, se je skrčila okoli niti. Magnetni loki so padali drug čez drugega, ne kot kletka, vsiljena od zunaj, temveč kot roka, ki se zapira nad lastnim darilom. Nit se je razpršila v bled sij, pretanek, da bi poškodoval ozračje ali jadro. Enajst tisoč let zbrane snovi se je razpršilo v svetlobo, ki je ne bi podedovala nobena meglica.
Raztrgani demonstrator je neškodljivo odneslo mimo Harrowa. Instrumenti Krone so izmerili rezultat: manj sevanja kot med navadno zimsko nevihto.
Rian je odmaknila roko s tretjega ključa.
Sael šest minut ni spregovorila.

**Tavi Sen**  
Lahko bi pustila, da ga prevzamejo odklonilniki.

**Sael**  
Dva sta bila budna. Eden je čakal, da me spozna.

**Tavi Sen**  
Jaz sem čakal, da spoznam tebe.

**Sael**  
Zdaj sva oba zapravila nekaj nenadomestljivega zaradi negotovosti drugega.
Tavi se je enkrat zasmejal, brez sape. To ni bilo odpuščanje, vendar je bil prvi zvok v izmenjavi, ki ni pripadal ne strahu ne veličini.
Rian je ponovno sklicala Harrowovo glasovanje. Aro je prosil, naj spregovori pred njim.

**Aro Venn**  
Dve postaji Krone ohranite kot odklonilnika. Grlno tuljavo stalite za polno jadro. Dogovor obnovite vsakih enajst let, natančno tako, kot je bilo predlagano. Če katera skupščina odstopi, Sael začasno ustavi naslednji sunek. Če Sael prekrši mejo zajema, postaji zaščitita lune.

**Sael**  
Še vedno se pripravljate proti meni.

**Aro Venn**  
Da. Ohranimo oba ščita. Dogovor znova preizkusimo čez enajst let.
Lok nad Saelino površino se je dvignil in umiril.

**Sael**  
Ohranite ščita Lume in Veya.

Harrow je z enainšestdesetimi odstotki glasoval za jadro. Tavi je glasoval za, potem ko je bil sklad za strehe habitatov prenesen na račun pod nadzorom vzhodnih zadrug. Rian je izdala ukaz. Livarski rezalniki so vstopili v črno grlno tuljavo in orožje tišine začeli spreminjati v štirideset trakov poslušajoče kovine. Delali so v treh izmenah in v vsak trak prenesli vzorec popravljenega šiva z demonstratorja, da so nadomestili pet dni, ki jih je stalo izenačeno glasovanje.

scenes.title: Dar, ki ga je mogoče zavrniti
paragraphs: *Prvo sončno jadro onkraj Harrowa · dan praga in štirideset ur pozneje*

Polno jadro se je proti Sael odprlo kot temna cvetlica. Štirideset trakov je bilo spojenih z obročem, zgrajenim iz grlne tuljave. Običajni vlačilci so držali devetintrideset. Illuminara je držala zadnjega, medtem ko so Rianine ekipe čez dvesto kilometrov mreže popravljale vzorec okvarjenega šiva z demonstratorja.
Po enainšestdesetih sekundah je Illuminara izpustila okvir.
Ostal je odprt.

Navijanja še ni bilo. Dokaz je ostal tisti, o katerem je glasoval Harrow: zajem najmanj devetindevetdeset celih sedem odstotka, nobena luna izpostavljena močnejšemu sevanju od navadne nevihte in smer, ki jo lahko zadržijo lovilci. Vse tri skupščine, livarski ceh in Sael so obdržali vsak svoj znak za ustavitev. Postaji Krone na Lume in Veyu sta čakali kot ščita, njuni globokopoljski vezji pa sta bili razstavljeni.

**Wren**  
Vse strani kažejo zeleno. Sael, pot lahko začneš in končaš.

**Sael**  
Ni samo moja.

Topel pritisk se je dotaknil jadra. Najprej je prispel ogljik, nato kisik, silicij in tanka svetla nit železa. Mreža je njihove naboje razvrstila v ugnezdene pasove, medtem ko je jantarna svetloba prečkala nočno stran vsake lune.

Inducirani tok jadra se je izlil v Harrowovo vzhodno omrežje. V najstarejši votlini so tiskalniki sevalnih streh začeli delati mesece pred popravljenim rokom. Tavi je z vlačilca opazoval njihov obremenitveni graf, eno roko pa še vedno držal nad zakrpanim šivom.

Črta zajema se je povzpela čez rdečo oznako. Izgubljeni delež se je razpršil nad ravnino luninih orbit, sevanje pa je ostalo pod ravnjo zimske nevihte. Lovilna jadra so eno za drugim prevzela ločene pasove in začela dolg zavoj proti Orielu.
Še vedno ni nihče navijal. Prikaz smeri je potreboval štirideset ur, da bi ločil stabilno pot od čudovite napake.

Sael je čakanje izkoristila za upočasnitev globljega magnetnega loka. Alarm za evakuacijo je ugasnil okrožje za okrožjem, vendar delo v zvezdi ni bilo tiho. Velike zanke, ki jih je Sael urejala dolga obdobja, so se sesedale v neškodljivo svetlobo.

**Sael**  
V enem dnevu sem nosila vse, kar sem razumela kot starševstvo. Zdaj to razstavljam plast za plastjo. Vaši instrumenti temu pravijo varnost. Ne znajo poimenovati tega, kar izginja.
Illuminara ni odgovorila z novo zasnovo. Wren je prosila, naj navigacijsko stražo preda Aru, odprla isto omejeno sončno okno, ki ga je Sael lahko končala, in ostala, ko se je prvi lok zrušil.

**Illuminara**  
Potem naj bom priča, ne da bi to preimenovala. Povej mi, kaj naj bi vsak del postal.

Skoraj eno uro ji Sael ni kazala prihodnjih ljudi, samo predvidene elemente, pritiske in razdalje. Ena sesedla zanka je bila uglašena tako, da bi železo poslala zadnje v vrteče se jedro mladega sveta in tako ohranila njegov prvi ocean topel pod bledim soncem. Illuminara je zaporedje ohranila, ne da bi ga skrčila, in vprašala, zakaj mora železo prispeti za silikati. Sael ji je časovno zaporedje pokazala dvakrat.

Ko se je okno zaprlo, so skupščinski prikazi kazali tri ločene enajstletne zaveze, vsako z lastno lučko za obnovitev. Zagovorniki meglice so sedeli ob stanovanjskih zadrugah, Sael in vsaka luna pa so obdržali znak za ustavitev.

V devetintrideseti uri je načrtovani tok začel zanašati. Na prikazu so ugnezdeni pasovi stopili vstran v istem ritmu, ki ga je Illuminara začutila v Sael: sunek se je spominjal magnetne zanke, ki ga je sprostila.

**Illuminara**  
Ni zapustil točke. Zanka se je pod njim obrnila. Aro, uporabi zadnji kot, ki ga je Sael pokazala jadru.
Aro je obrat že polagal čez geometrijo lovilcev. Njegov popravek je drugo jadro zadržal znotraj njegovega preostalega dosega.

**Aro Venn**  
Drugi lovilec ga še lahko zadrži, če nam Sael da končni kot zanke.

**Sael**  
Nameravate izboljšati mojo smer.

**Aro Venn**  
Nameravam preprečiti, da bi tvoje darilo postalo prazno vreme.
Sael je poslala kot. Aro je poslal popravek. Po štiridesetih urah so se tri lovilna jadra ustalila na stabilni poti, katere stožec negotovosti je v celoti ležal znotraj Orielove vodikove police.

Takrat je sistem zavriskal. Začelo se je v Livarni devet, kjer so rezalniki z orodjem udarjali po praznih nosilcih Krone. Razširilo se je po skupščinskih galerijah in bolnišničnih hodnikih. Doseglo je staro votlino, ko je prvi strešni panel vroč prišel iz tiskalnika. Celo prevajalnik je vibracije prenesel nazaj Sael.

**Sael**  
Ali tako zvenijo potniki, ko odločajo, kam gre plovilo?

**Illuminara**  
Poslušaj jih. Smer so izbrali s teboj.

**Sael**  
Ne imenuj tihih svetov manj resničnih zdaj, ko si rešila govoreče.

**Illuminara**  
Ne bom. Ti pa govorečih nikoli več ne imenuj potniki.
Sael je za odgovor potrebovala sedem človeških sekund, zavestno zamudo uma, ki bi lahko uporabljal stoletja.

**Sael**  
Posadka, torej. Težavna posadka.

Prvi sunek je bil premajhen, da bi ustvaril planet, in nihče ni mogel dokazati, da se bo Oriel kdaj prebudil. Štirje odstotki Orisonovih livarn bodo služili verigi. Sael bo umrla prej, kot so si želele lune. Aro je obdržal dva ščita, ker ena pogumna odločitev ni izbrisala razloga, zaradi katerega ju je zgradil. Tavijevo družino je čakalo še več mesecev gradnje strehe.
Wren je Illuminari našla sedečo na trupu observatorija, ko je praznovanje že pojenjalo, z obema rokama na topli kovini. Wren ni rekla ničesar; dlan je položila poleg ene od Illuminaričinih.
Sael je z Arovo navigacijsko ekipo popravljala naslednji sunek; vsak popravek je skozi kovino prihajal kot nizko, toplo brnenje. Daleč onkraj pogleda so tri majhna jadra držala smer proti Orielu.

translation_sl.critic_line: Sael, zvezda, ki je šest milijard let osvetljevala tri naseljene lune, ni niti utišana niti prisiljena v enodnevni izbruh: Illuminaričino razumevanje tega, kar je hotela zapustiti za seboj, postane ustavljiv sunek, ki ga lune lahko obnovijo ali končajo, prva lovilna jadra pa obdržijo smer proti Orielu.
